Annopol Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Annopol, Poland

Demolished. Annopol was originally the village of Rachów, called that until the 18th century, though development had already begun before 1740. By 1939, Jews made up an extraordinary 73 percent of the town's population. During the 1942 liquidation of the Annopol Ghetto, some Jews were murdered near the town and the rest deported to Kraśnik, documented elsewhere in this collection, and then to the Bełżec death camp; a separate mass execution in 1943 is commemorated by a memorial on Skały Street. This, Annopol's first Jewish cemetery, was established within the synagogue complex, likely in the mid-18th century, and used until around 1800, when a new cemetery opened. Totally destroyed during WWII, it fell into disrepair afterward; in the 1970s, town authorities liquidated the site entirely and built a health center and kindergarten on it.
